solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Are sheep the booty in these types of burglary?

definitions.text: Are sheep the booty in these types of burglary?

parts.words: Are sheep the booty in these types of burglary?
parts.note: read literally, the phrase for smash-and-grab break-ins describes raids carried out to steal male sheep

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether thieves are out rustling livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: A ram raid is a British term for a burglary in which a vehicle is driven through a shop front; the clue pretends the 'ram' is the loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimes where a vehicle smashes through a shopfront are known by this British term, and taken literally it means raids for rams.

clue.text: Rogues held hand bombs and acted without thinking

indicators.note: a thing that bombs is blown apart, so the letters of the three words before it are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Villains clutching grenades behaved recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombs' looks like a noun the rogues are holding, but it is a verb signalling the anagram of ROGUES HELD HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge in impetuously, without stopping to consider, is to behave rashly and without reflection.

clue.text: Beggar cannot be seen chasing designer denim

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the anagram
designer suggests something made or reworked, so the letters of denim are rearranged

parts.note: cannot contracts to can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A beggar can't be seen wearing expensive designer jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designer' reads as a label on the jeans, but it signals the anagram; 'be seen chasing' means the contraction comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is a person, often a friar, who lives by asking for alms, so a synonym for one who begs.

clue.text: Northbound Melbourne river formation

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards, so the river's name is written backwards

parts.note: the Yarra is the river flowing through Melbourne, Australia

explanation.surface: A river in Melbourne flows north in some pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northbound' turns YARRA round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an ordered arrangement, such as troops drawn up in ranks, so a formation.

clue.text: Fellow holding papers? That won't happen

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other, so the university man wraps round the paper

parts.note: a don is a fellow or tutor at a university college
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: An academic clutching his papers is told his hopes are doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' is the Oxbridge sense of a college academic, and 'papers' a quantity of sheets rather than documents.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sarcastic retort telling someone their hope is a fantasy, i.e. it will never come true.

clue.text: Soup served in club or school

indicators.note: served in says the dish lies inside the run of words, spanning club, or and school

explanation.surface: A soup is on the menu at a club or a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' signals that the answer sits within cluB OR SCHool.
explanation.definitionFit: Borsch is a beetroot soup from Eastern Europe, also spelt borscht.

clue.text: Supervision error

definitions.meaning: the sense of watching over or managing others' work
the sense of a mistake made by failing to notice something

explanation.surface: A slip in supervision.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has two contrary senses: control and management of work, and a careless mistake or omission.

clue.text: Shooter has no right to get bird

indicators.note: having no of something means it is removed, so the abbreviation for right comes out

parts.note: a sniper is a hidden marksman

explanation.surface: A marksman with no rights is allowed to shoot a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes R from SNIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The snipe is a wading bird with a long bill, the original target of the sniper.

clue.text: Darling models new strange fruit

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment like darling

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or altered, so the letters of models new are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is modelling some unusual new fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' shuffles MODELS NEW into DEW MELONS, after HONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: These sweet melons with pale green flesh are a familiar variety of fruit.

clue.text: After rain soaks bits and pieces

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the phrase says the ... what the rain has soaked

explanation.surface: After rain soaks some odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: split into SUN DRIES, it describes what happens once rain has drenched things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items not worth listing separately, so odds and ends.

clue.text: Stoop to embrace skinhead — that shows style

indicators.note: embracing means wrapping round, so the first letter of skin goes inside the verb for condescending

parts.note: to stoop to something is to deign, lower oneself to do it
the head of skin is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone lowers themselves to hug a skinhead, showing real panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' is not the youth subculture but the head of 'skin', S, which 'to embrace' puts inside DEIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a pattern or decorative scheme, i.e. the look or fashion of something.

clue.text: Previously one in a hundred, on the contrary

indicators.note: in would put one inside the other, the word for one inside the Roman hundred
this reverses the containment, so the Roman hundred goes inside the word for one instead

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Formerly it was a one-in-a-hundred chance, or rather the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' would put ONE inside C; 'on the contrary' flips it, putting C inside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, formerly, so a synonym for previously.

clue.text: Make divine switch of leaders to illuminate

indicators.note: the leaders are the first two letters of the word, and switching them swaps their places

parts.note: to deify is to make into a god

explanation.surface: Swapping some leaders would make things divine and enlighten everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch of leaders' swaps the first two letters of DEIFY, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct and improve someone morally or intellectually, so to enlighten them.

clue.text: Second queen to be held captive in horrid abbey

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: being held captive in something means sitting inside it, so the queen goes within the word for horrid

parts.note: nasty means horrid, unpleasant
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a standard abbreviation for the queen

explanation.surface: A queen is held prisoner for a second time in a horrible abbey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal but is a short moment; 'to be held captive in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a religious community's house of monks, so a kind of cloister.

clue.text: Aging criminal giant chasing vehicle with secret agent

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the anagram comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
James Bond is the fictional secret agent

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of giant are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An old crooked giant is chasing a car carrying a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aging' looks like an adjective for the giant, but it is the definition, a gerund for working out age; 'criminal' is the anagram signal and 'chasing' puts it last.
explanation.definitionFit: This radiocarbon method establishes how old organic material is, so it is a technique for working out an object's age.

clue.text: Go at last, you need love and bliss

parts.note: beat it! is a slang command meaning go away

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each of the following three words

explanation.surface: Go at last, because love is what you need for happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is BEAT IT; 'at last' takes the final letters of 'you need love', U, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatitude means supreme blessedness or happiness, the state of perfect joy.

clue.text: We're leaving this mythical being for a minor royal

parts.note: the UK voted to leave the European Union, the EU
a genie is a magical spirit from Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A spirit decides to depart, standing in for a junior member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We're leaving this' alludes to Brexit, the UK's departure from the European Union, giving EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Eugenie is a granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II, well down the line of succession.

clue.text: Useless aristocrat, awfully vain inside

indicators.note: inside places the jumbled letters within the word for aristocrat

parts.note: a noble is a member of the aristocracy

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of vain are mixed up

explanation.surface: A worthless lord is terribly conceited at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' is the anagram signal on vain, and 'inside' places the result within the aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonviable cannot work or survive, so it is of no practical use.

clue.text: See 1
Additional court passage

parts.note: extra means additional

explanation.surface: An additional passageway to the court.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a short section taken from a book or piece of music, so an excerpt.

clue.text: Ingredient of oriental curry powder

indicators.note: Ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dusting of something goes into an Eastern curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine dusting substance for the skin.

clue.text: See 14
Staggering day, for a stranger

indicators.note: one word standing for another means a substitution, so the comparative of odd replaces the letter a

parts.note: taken as written
odder means stranger

explanation.surface: A stranger is reeling for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' says ODDER stands in place of the A in DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery describes someone shaky and unsteady on their feet, typically through age, so tottering.

clue.text: See 8
Expired, yet intrinsically pure

indicators.note: intrinsically means within, so the word for yet sits inside the word for expired

parts.note: died means expired
still means yet, as in 'still waiting'

explanation.surface: Something passed away, yet was fundamentally innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intrinsically' is the container signal; 'yet' is an adverb meaning even now, not a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled water or spirit has been purified by evaporation and condensation, so it is free of contaminants.

clue.text: Calm needed to make whisky, in 23

definitions.meaning: the sense of motionless, quiet, tranquil
the sense of apparatus for distilling spirits

explanation.surface: Calm is needed to make whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 23' is a bonus nod: the answer is found inside DISTILLED at 23 across, where it served as 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tranquil and unmoving, and it is also the apparatus a distiller uses to produce spirits.

clue.text: Whisper fanciful ideas

indicators.note: fanciful suggests something imaginatively reworked, so the letters of ideas are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs some far-fetched notions.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark spoken quietly so that only some hear, as in a stage whisper.

clue.text: Empty nook in beer joint

indicators.note: in places the outer letters of nook inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: an empty word loses its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A deserted corner of a pub serving beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' keeps only the outside letters of nook and 'in' is the container signal; 'joint' suggests a pub but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge connecting the foot to the leg, one of the body's articulations.

clue.text: Tuneful, without Mel becoming offensive

indicators.note: without means going without, so the name is taken away from the word for tuneful

parts.note: melodious means tuneful
taken as written, the name Mel

explanation.surface: Musical without Mel, the act turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes MEL from the start of MELODIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repulsive, so thoroughly unpleasant.

clue.text: Keep going round a boot, mostly in infantile game

indicators.note: going round means turning back on itself, so the word keep is read backwards
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of boot is dropped

explanation.surface: Keep circling the boot of a car in a childish game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the reversal signal, and 'mostly' means all but the last letter of boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is the game in which you hide your face and then reveal it to amuse a baby.

clue.text: Kitchen not right place for art

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for right is struck out

parts.note: a gallery is where art is exhibited

explanation.surface: A kitchen is the wrong place to hang art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R from GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the cooking area on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Bonfire spotted back in range

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word for spotted is written in reverse

parts.note: seen means spotted, noticed

explanation.surface: A bonfire is spotted back in the mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal; 'range' means a chain of mountains, not a cooker or a spread.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the mountain chain dividing France from Spain.
